questions.enonce_markdown: For each method, name a suitable salt and describe how a pure dry sample is prepared in the laboratory. *[18 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**1. Neutralisation (acid + alkali): sodium chloride.**

$\mathrm{NaOH(aq) + HCl(aq) \rightarrow NaCl(aq) + H_2O(l)}$

- Using a pipette, put $25.0\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of sodium hydroxide solution in a conical flask and add 2 drops of methyl orange (yellow).

- Run in dilute hydrochloric acid from a burette until the indicator just turns orange (the end point); record the volume of acid.

- Repeat with the same volumes of alkali and acid but **without indicator**, because the indicator would contaminate the salt.

- Heat the solution in an evaporating dish until it is saturated (a drop on a cold glass rod forms crystals); leave it to cool and crystallise.

- Filter off the crystals, wash with a very little cold distilled water, and dry them between filter papers or in a warm oven.

**2. Action of a dilute acid on a metal: zinc sulphate** (from zinc, a metal of moderate reactivity; sodium and potassium are too violent, copper and silver do not react).

$\mathrm{Zn(s) + H_2SO_4(aq) \rightarrow ZnSO_4(aq) + H_2(g)}$

- Warm dilute sulphuric acid in a beaker and add **excess zinc** in small amounts until effervescence stops (all the acid is used up).

- Filter to remove the unreacted zinc; the filtrate is zinc sulphate solution.

- Heat the filtrate to evaporate it to the crystallisation point, cool slowly, filter off the crystals, wash with a little cold distilled water and dry them between filter papers.

**3. Double decomposition (precipitation) of an insoluble salt: barium sulphate.**

$\mathrm{BaCl_2(aq) + Na_2SO_4(aq) \rightarrow BaSO_4(s) + 2NaCl(aq)}$

- Mix solutions of barium chloride and sodium sulphate (a soluble barium salt and a soluble sulphate); a white precipitate of barium sulphate forms at once.

- Filter the mixture, and wash the residue on the filter paper with distilled water to remove the soluble sodium chloride.

- Dry the residue between filter papers or in a warm oven.

(All the equations are balanced: for example, in the last one Ba 1, Cl 2, Na 2, S 1, O 4 on both sides.)

questions.enonce_markdown: State two physical properties of any of the named salts. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
For **sodium chloride**: it is a white crystalline solid, and it is soluble in water (it also has a high melting point, about $801^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$).

For **barium sulphate**: it is a white powder, and it is insoluble in water.
